blocks.title: Runtime Errors
bullets: Runtime errors refer to those created by unexpected behavior within your code. For example, perhaps you intended for a user to input a number, but they input a character instead.

blocks.title: Runtime Errors Example
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Runtime Errors
bullets: As programmers, we should be defensive to ensure that our users are entering what we expected. We might consider "corner cases" such as `-1`, `0`, or `cat`.
If we run this program and type in "cat", we'll suddenly see `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'cat'`.
An effective strategy to fix this potential error would be to create "error handling" to ensure the user behaves as we intend.

rightPanel.label: Code Example

blocks.question: Does an if-else statement always execute exactly one branch?
blocks.answer: Yes! If the condition is True, the 'if' branch runs. If False, the 'else' branch runs. They never run together.
